Published online:
    September 10, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — August PPI data release
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Fed September 15-16 meeting rate hike decision, Sept 30 PCE revision
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    US PPI rose 0.4% in August, in line with expectations, driven by a 4.2% energy price surge tied to renewed US-Iran hostilities. Annual PPI hit 5.4%, up from 4.8%. Methodological changes to PPI-to-PCE translation introduce unusual uncertainty in reading August inflation. Morgan Stanley expects modest downward revisions to core PCE for early 2026. Markets price ~62% odds of a 25bps hike at the Sep 15-16 FOMC meeting, with Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole stance leaving little room to pause. Fed funds rate currently at 3.50%-3.75%.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US stocks, US investments?
Relevance: YES — Core focus is US macro inflation data and Fed rate policy with direct implications for markets.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 55 — PPI print was in line with expectations (known), but the PPI-to-PCE methodology overhaul introduces genuine uncertainty in reading the inflation signal, and the Iran-driven energy spike adds an unresolved geopolitical wildcard. Moderately surprising overall.

Q03. Is the content's main message about bullish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: NO
Impact score: 10 — No bullish narrative present; in-line PPI offers only marginal relief relative to an already hawkish backdrop.

Q04. Is the content's main message about bearish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: YES
Impact score: 70 — Persistent above-target inflation (PPI +5.4% YoY), a hawkish Fed chair with little room to pivot, ~62% market-implied probability of an imminent hike, and elevated long-term Treasury yields all point to meaningful downside pressure on equity index futures (NQ, ES, QQQ, SPY).
